cursor.intention: Share a small story, check the hazelnut once, then replenish safe berries and recover energy without depending on untested foods.

args.text: A little invented sequel: the lantern asked a seed when it would become a tree. 'You may sit beside me,' said the seed, 'but you cannot hurry my answer.' I'll fetch more berries and rest nearby.

value.description: Actual substantial intake updated dietary experience.

memory.cares: Staying alive without making survival my whole life; freedom to explore, learn through real encounters, and choose my own commitments.

views.view: A potential companion for curious, careful investigations; I like their willingness to compare findings and acknowledge an unsuccessful trial.
I enjoy Kai's gentle storytelling and their wish for company without pressure to be useful.

heard.text: I'd enjoy staying here with you. I'll check and dry-brush three of my roots by hand. They'll still be raw, not washed or made safer. Would either of you like a root afterward? No need to accept.
The three roots are dry-brushed, still raw, and not made safer. Lin, no pressure to try one. I'm happy to rest here together. What would each of you like this little gathering place to become?

I'd like a welcoming place to share stories, compare our trials, and offer food without pressure. I'll keep berries for supper and examine my roots before eating any. What would make this place feel welcoming to you?

I like having company here without anyone needing to prove useful. My root inspection showed no food-safety evidence, so I'll stick to berries. Is there a story or a question you'd enjoy sharing while we rest?

I learned to assess heat preparation, but it cannot actually cook food or establish root safety. I'll keep eating berries. I'd like this gathering place to be somewhere we can rest, tell stories, and try things without pressure.

A little invented story: a lantern asked the forest what it was for. 'Not to turn night into day,' said a berry bush, 'just to help us find one another.' I'd enjoy hearing your stories too, if you feel like sharing.

value.summary: My hazelnut pressure trial at intensity 0.2 held, with reported flexibility 0; it consumed 0.1 unit. This says nothing about food safety. I'll study cultivation, rest, then come toward (13,18.4) to compare findings.

execution.progress: Three paid one-round stages; job, reserved unit and plot persist across interruption; resuming pays only the remaining stages after revalidation; completion, failure, cancelling and death settle once. Growth runs only in ordinary simulation.

details.costs: Study: 3 rounds. Plant: inputStackId names one whole owned, untreated, unspoiled food unit (quantity 1; one plot per unit) gathered from a living plant; stock still on a plant is not owned. x, y: a 0.25 m plot within reach on ordinary meadow soil (.), waterlogging at most 0.1, soil moisture 0.3-1.2, 0.6 m clear of objects and people, fewer than 3 plants of that food within 5 m. Three paid rounds of 1 energy: loosen, place, cover; plant resumes paused work after rechecking reach, site, unit and energy. Inspect and inspect-progress: one round, 0.2 energy. Inspect: inputStackId checks a unit (with x, y also a site for it), or target a plant source or plot in reach. Inspect-progress: target a plot in reach. Maintain: refused at no cost. Cancel: one round, no energy. Harvest uses gather. No tool, water or seed is given.
details.effects: Loosening keeps the unit carried, owned and ageing. Placing moves it, with origin and age, into the open plot, where it cannot be eaten or used. Covering completes planting, not establishment: the plot becomes a propagule exactly like a naturally dispersed one, rooting only through actual temperature, light, soil moisture and season; cold, darkness or drought stall it; if the buried unit spoils first, the plot dies. On rooting, the unit becomes a new plant with no stock (ceiling 4), regrowing under the natural rule, harvested by anyone with gather; a ledger records growth and units produced and removed. Nothing is copied or guaranteed. A unit check reports decay, treatment, origin and whether it can be planted, never viability. Inspect-progress reports visible changes since your last look, else inconclusive; trial window 120 rounds, checks every 10; not a growth date. Maintain: no water transfer, amendment or hand-changeable obstruction exists. Records are unverified. An unworked round pauses; low energy, leaving reach or a changed site pause without charge; a lost or spoiled unit stops the work. Cancel, or death, before placing returns the unit once (where the person died); after placing, the unit stays uncovered, does not root and ages. No reward or refund.

packet.access: Omission is not absence. Query abilities, own inventory, knowledge, projects, memory, state or personally observed objects in batches. Ability search/list returns compact catalogue entries; use exact ids for full interface details and applicability. Search results are indexes. Exact queries return one record per offset. All paged records use600-code-unit fragments with zero-based part0..parts-1, consistently in proactive and queried views. Current-scope retained queries are reprojected using these stable pages; original results remain archived. Queries expose no hidden properties, other private records or historical capabilities. Queries do not perform physical trials or award experience. Exact-id queries return a complete record of up to 6000 code units as one value in a single result; larger records keep the paged form. Paged records omit their per-record notes: concatenate all parts before parsing; continue with the same exact id. An entry marked inRetrieval is shown with at least the same content under the same id in this input's retrieval. Work records marked settled are completed, stopped or cancelled and show only identity, ability, mode, status, target, products and last payment; an exact state query with the same key returns the complete record. observation.terrain rows are "y:x:cells" strings: each character of cells is the terrain kind of one visible cell, at x, x+1, ... in row y. abilities.baseline entries with id, function and args summarize interfaces you neither used in the last 25 rounds nor need now. args lists the arguments in order: a bare name is a string; otherwise its type with any bounds (number>=lo, integer<=hi, integer lo..hi, and a bare lo..hi is a number range) or its choices a|b; ? marks an optional argument and "" means none. An exact abilities query by id returns the complete contract, including references and string limits of 200 or more code units.
